issue_title: Redis backend: AsyncResult.__del__ deadlocks apply_async() by re-entering PubSub._lock
issue_body:
# Checklist - [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `main` branch of Celery. - [ ] This has already been asked to the [discussions forum](https://github.com/celery/celery/discussions) first. - [x] I have read the relevant section in the [contribution guide](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/main/contributing.html#other-bugs) on reporting bugs. - [x] I have checked the [issues list](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22Issue+Type%3A+Bug+Report%22+-label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22) for similar or identical bug reports. - [x] I have checked the [pull requests list](https://github.com/celery/celery/pulls?q=is%3Apr+label%3A%22PR+Type%3A+Bugfix%22+-label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22) for existing proposed fixes. - [x] I have checked the [commit log](https://github.com/celery/celery/commits/main) to find out if the bug was already fixed in the main branch. - [x] I have included all related issues and possible duplicate issues in this issue (If there are none, check this box anyway). - [ ] I have tried to reproduce the issue with [pytest-celery](https://docs.celeryq.dev/projects/pytest-celery/en/latest/userguide/celery-bug-report.html) and added the reproduction script below. > Notes on the two unchecked boxes, for transparency: this was not raised in Discussions first because there is a deterministic reproduction script and a production stack trace, so there was no open question to discuss. The reproduction is a standalone script rather than a `pytest-celery` case because it needs to control garbage-collection timing precisely; it requires only a Redis server and no worker. > > "Verified against `main`" means: reproduced on 5.6.3 (latest release), and the three implicated functions — `AsyncResult.__del__`, `ResultConsumer.cancel_for`, `RedisBackend.on_task_call` — are byte-identical on `main` as of 2026-08-12. ## Mandatory Debugging Information - [x] I have included the output of ``celery -A proj report`` in the issue. - [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `main` branch of Celery. - [x] I have included the contents of ``pip freeze`` in the issue. - [x] I have included all the versions of all the external dependencies required to reproduce this bug. ## Optional Debugging Information - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one Python version and/or implementation. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one message broker and/or result backend. - [x] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one version of the message broker and/or result backend. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one operating system. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one workers pool. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue with autoscaling, retries, ETA/Countdown & rate limits disabled. - [x] I have tried reproducing the issue after downgrading and/or upgrading Celery and its dependencies. ## Related Issues and Possible Duplicates #### Related Issues - #6969 — same class of deadlock (GC finalizer vs. `threading.Lock` in the Redis backend), closed unmerged as a redis-py issue. Different trigger: `PubSub.__del__` during *disconnection*, not `AsyncResult.__del__` during an in-flight `SUBSCRIBE`. - #6963 — the Redis result consumer is not drained, so unsubscribes accumulate. Same machinery, resource-leak symptom rather than deadlock. - #4707 — no unsubscribe from `celery-task-meta-*` channels when `ignore_result=True`. #### Possible Duplicates - None ## Environment & Settings **Celery version**: 5.6.3 (also reproduced on 5.6.2)
celery report Output:

``` software -> celery:5.6.3 (recovery) kombu:5.6.2 py:3.11.15 billiard:4.2.4 redis:6.3.0 platform -> system:Darwin arch:64bit kernel version:25.5.0 imp:CPython loader -> celery.loaders.app.AppLoader settings -> transport:redis results:redis://localhost:6379/0 broker_url: 'redis://localhost:6379/0' result_backend: 'redis://localhost:6379/0' deprecated_settings: None ```

# Steps to Reproduce ## Required Dependencies - **Minimal Python Version**: 3.11 - **Minimal Celery Version**: reproduced on 5.6.2 and 5.6.3; implicated code is unchanged on `main` - **Minimal Kombu Version**: 5.6.2 - **Minimal Broker Version**: any Redis (broker is irrelevant — the deadlock is in the result backend) - **Minimal Result Backend Version**: any Redis - **Minimal OS and/or Kernel Version**: N/A (reproduced on macOS; originally observed on Linux/aarch64) - **Minimal Broker Client Version**: N/A - **Minimal Result Backend Client Version**: **redis-py <= 6.3.0** (see below — 6.4.0 is unaffected) ### Python Packages
pip freeze Output:

``` amqp==5.3.1 billiard==4.2.4 celery==5.6.3 click==8.4.2 click-didyoumean==0.3.1 click-plugins==1.1.1.2 click-repl==0.3.0 kombu==5.6.2 packaging==26.3 prompt_toolkit==3.0.53 PyJWT==2.13.0 python-dateutil==2.9.0.post0 redis==6.3.0 six==1.17.0 tzdata==2026.3 tzlocal==5.4.4 vine==5.1.0 wcwidth==0.8.2 ```

### Other Dependencies

A Redis server. No worker is required to reproduce. **redis-py version is decisive:** | redis-py | `PubSub._lock` | Result | |---|---|---| | 5.3.1 – 6.3.0 | `threading.Lock()` | **deadlocks** | | 6.4.0 | `threading.RLock()` | does not deadlock | redis-py 6.4.0 changed `PubSub._lock` to a reentrant lock, which masks this. On any earlier redis-py, Celery self-deadlocks.

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

```python """Celery deadlock: AsyncResult.__del__ re-enters the Redis pubsub lock during a publish. REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0 python celery_mre.py Requires only a Redis server; no worker. Exits non-zero and dumps the deadlocked stack if reproduced. """ import faulthandler import gc import os import signal import sys import redis import redis.connection from celery import Celery REDIS = os.environ.get("REDIS_URL", "redis://localhost:6379/0") HANG_SECONDS = 15 app = Celery("mre", broker=REDIS, backend=REDIS) @app.task def noop(x): return x def _on_alarm(signum, frame): print(f"\n=== REPRODUCED: publish did not return within {HANG_SECONDS}s ===\n", flush=True) faulthandler.dump_traceback() sys.exit(1) def main(): import celery print(f"celery={celery.__version__} redis-py={redis.__version__}", flush=True) # Keep the finalizable result alive until we collect explicitly, below. gc.disable() result = noop.apply_async(args=(1,)) # What AsyncResult.get() does internally: start the ResultConsumer and SUBSCRIBE. app.backend.add_pending_result(result) # Fulfilment drops the backend's strong reference. In real code this happens when # the result arrives and .get() returns; the AsyncResult is then reachable only # from user code, and its __del__ will call remove_pending_result a second time. app.backend.remove_pending_result(result) # A reference cycle, so refcounting cannot free it at a safe point and # finalization is deferred to the cyclic collector. cycle = {"result": result} cycle["self"] = cycle del result, cycle # Simulate a collection landing inside the socket write, while PubSub._lock is held. # This happens naturally whenever a GC lands in that window. original_send = redis.connection.AbstractConnection.send_packed_command def send_packed_command(self, *args, **kwargs): gc.collect() return original_send(self, *args, **kwargs) redis.connection.AbstractConnection.send_packed_command = send_packed_command signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _on_alarm) signal.alarm(HANG_SECONDS) print("publishing (deadlocks here)...", flush=True) noop.apply_async(args=(2,)) signal.alarm(0) print("published OK -- not reproduced", flush=True) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```

# Expected Behavior `apply_async()` publishes the task and returns, regardless of whether a garbage collection happens to run during the call. More generally: `AsyncResult.__del__` should not perform blocking network I/O. A finalizer can run at any allocation point, including inside a critical section that already holds the lock the finalizer will need. # Actual Behavior `apply_async()` never returns. The process hangs forever with no error, no timeout and no log output. `RedisBackend.on_task_call()` runs on every `send_task()` and issues a PUBSUB `SUBSCRIBE`. redis-py's `PubSub.execute_command()` holds `self._lock` across the socket write. If a garbage collection lands inside that write and finalizes an `AsyncResult`, the finalizer re-acquires the same lock on the same thread: ``` apply_async → send_task → on_task_call (celery/backends/redis.py) → consume_from → _consume_from → subscribe (redis/client.py) → execute_command → with self._lock: ← ACQUIRED → send_command → send_packed_command → sendall → [garbage collection] → AsyncResult.__del__ (celery/result.py) → backend.remove_pending_result (celery/backends/asynchronous.py) → on_result_fulfilled → ResultConsumer.cancel_for (celery/backends/redis.py) → pubsub.unsubscribe (redis/client.py) → execute_command → with self._lock: ← SAME THREAD → DEADLOCK ``` Stack from the reproduction script (`faulthandler`, most recent call first): ``` Current thread (most recent call first): Garbage-collecting File ".../redis/client.py", line 858 in execute_command File ".../redis/client.py", line 1043 in unsubscribe File ".../celery/backends/redis.py", line 187 in cancel_for File ".../celery/backends/asynchronous.py", line 261 in on_result_fulfilled File ".../celery/backends/asynchronous.py", line 253 in remove_pending_result File ".../celery/result.py", line 419 in __del__ File ".../redis/connection.py", line 577 in send_command File ".../redis/client.py", line 903 in File ".../redis/retry.py", line 62 in call_with_retry File ".../redis/client.py", line 902 in _execute File ".../redis/client.py", line 859 in execute_command File ".../redis/client.py", line 1018 in subscribe File ".../celery/backends/redis.py", line 180 in _consume_from File ".../celery/backends/redis.py", line 173 in consume_from File ".../celery/backends/redis.py", line 417 in on_task_call File ".../celery/app/base.py", line 946 in send_task File ".../celery/app/task.py", line 608 in apply_async ``` ### This is not synthetic — it happens in production We hit this five times over six days in production (Celery 5.6.2, redis-py 5.3.1, Python 3.11.15, Linux aarch64, AWS ElastiCache over TLS). Each time a Prefect flow process hung permanently at `group(...).apply_async()`; the work was never dispatched and the process sat in `futex_wait_queue` indefinitely. Below is a stack captured with `py-spy` from a **live production process that had been deadlocked for five days** — the same interleaving: ``` _work (our code) ← group(...).apply_async() apply_async (celery/canvas.py:1612) → _apply_tasks → chain → Signature send_task (celery/app/base.py:946) on_task_call (celery/backends/redis.py:417) consume_from → subscribe (redis/client.py:1018) send_packed_command (redis/connection.py:555) sendall (ssl.py:1270) ← mid-write, holding PubSub._lock __del__ (celery/result.py:419) remove_pending_result (asynchronous.py:253) on_result_fulfilled (asynchronous.py:261) cancel_for (celery/backends/redis.py:187) unsubscribe (redis/client.py:1043) execute_command (redis/client.py:858) ← blocked forever ``` `py-spy --locals` confirmed the finalized object was an `AsyncResult` for a task whose result had already been consumed and whose reference had gone out of scope. It is much easier to hit over TLS (`rediss://`), where the write is slower and allocates more, widening the window for a collection to land inside it. ### Notes on the mechanism Two details make this reachable in ordinary code: 1. `on_task_call()` subscribes on **every** `send_task()`, so every publish performs pub/sub I/O while holding the lock. The dangerous window is not narrow — it is entered on every task dispatch. 2. `cancel_for()` unsubscribes without checking whether the key is still in `subscribed_to`. It `discard()`s the key and then calls `unsubscribe()` regardless, so a second `remove_pending_result` for an already-fulfilled result still performs a network round-trip. That second call is the one that lands inside the publish. The application code that triggers this is unremarkable — publish a task, `get()` its result, drop the reference, publish another task: ```python r = some_task.apply_async() r.get() del r # or simply let it go out of scope other_task.apply_async() # ← may deadlock here ``` ### Suggested fix Do not perform network I/O in `AsyncResult.__del__`. Queue the unsubscribe for the drainer/result-consumer thread instead of issuing it inline from a finalizer — which is also where #6963 suggests draining should be happening. redis-py 6.4.0 changing `PubSub._lock` to an `RLock` prevents the hang, but that looks like mitigation rather than a fix: a reentrant `UNSUBSCRIBE` issued in the middle of a partially written `SUBSCRIBE` can still interleave bytes on the wire.
